title: AutoCAD Pricing 2026: LT vs Full Cost Per Year
summary: AutoCAD pricing for 2026 starts at $540 for LT or $2,095 for the full version annually. Paying monthly instead costs about $1,025 more per year.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and limits buyers hit after purchase


Beyond idle seats, the most visible leak, four other costs sit outside the price on the page: missing LT features, named-user rules, renewal increases, and add-on and hardware requirements.


> Seats that sit idle cost the same as seats in daily use, and trimming even a few of them beats most discounts.


Buy LT and you give up 3D modelling and programming interfaces, but you keep LISP routines (small scripts that automate repeat drawing tasks).


If a colleague's workflow or a plug-in depends on any of those, you find out after buying LT, and the fix is paying again for full AutoCAD.


Passing a login around to cover shifts or part-timers breaks the terms, because a subscription belongs to one named person, not to a desk. The safe fix is another seat. Count people who actually draw, not people who might.


That is per-seat pricing doing what it does: every added person becomes a charge, so licences go to a few and everyone else waits.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) charges for use instead, in credits, with one credit per run however many steps it has and unlimited flows on every plan including free, and Alan and Funding Societies run it in production.


Unless you cancel, subscriptions renew on their own, and **the renewal price can be higher** than what you first paid.


Do nothing and you'll pay the new rate for another full term. Put the renewal date in the calendar well ahead of time and re-check the plan then.


### AutoCAD add-on, storage and hardware costs


Specialised toolsets and extra cloud storage cost more on top of the base plan, so a plan that looked cheap can grow quickly.


Newer versions also expect reasonably current computers, and files saved in a recent version may not open for a client or subcontractor on an older one. Budget for a machine upgrade or a round of save-as conversions before either surprises you.
